source: Mālinīvijayottaratantra 2.21 (Kashmir Series 1922) via Svarodaya.org/upaya + Hareesh Tantrasāra ch.5
sanskrit: uccāra-karaṇa-dhyāna-varṇa-sthāna-prakalpanaiḥ / yo bhavet sa samāveśaḥ samyag āṇava ucyate //
en: The immersion that comes about through utterance of breath, instruments of body, visualisation, phonemes and fashioning of supports — that is rightly called āṇava.

components.en: breath / utterance / upward movement of sounded prāṇa

tantrasara_ch5.note: Āṇavopāya uses limited supports: imagination (buddhi), vital energy (prāṇa), body, ritual vessels. Five practices: dhyāna · uccāra (grosser) · phoneme (subtler prāṇa) · karaṇa · external objects.
tantrasara_ch5.quote: relying on those supports that have a specifically defined & limited nature—such as the imagination (buddhi), vital energy (prāṇa), the body, ritual vessels… one enters fully into one's individuated expression of Divinity

upaya_order_theory.note: Abhinavagupta presents from immediate recognition downward. Body/sound practice travels the opposite direction.
upaya_order_theory.justification: You're beginning at the end of his theoretical presentation because that part is designed for embodied practice (āṇava). Not bastardizing the system.
